evals.description: Happy path: steps.mem present, deps satisfied, no stale files. Verifies progress is updated, code-map appended, and step completes.
evals.setup:
mkdir -p /tmp/eval-act-0/.memplan/memory /tmp/eval-act-0/.memplan/decisions /tmp/eval-act-0/.memplan/inbox && echo '1/3 | write-layout' > /tmp/eval-act-0/.memplan/progress && printf '+step:id=1,text=write-layout,atomic=true
+step:id=2,text=write-cli-js,deps=1,atomic=true
+step:id=3,text=write-tests,deps=2,atomic=true
' > /tmp/eval-act-0/.memplan/steps.mem && touch /tmp/eval-act-0/.memplan/memory/code-map.mem /tmp/eval-act-0/.memplan/memory/entities.mem /tmp/eval-act-0/.memplan/memory/failures.mem && printf '' > /tmp/eval-act-0/.memplan/stale.mem && printf '' > /tmp/eval-act-0/.memplan/deps.mem && printf '' > /tmp/eval-act-0/.memplan/deps-closure.mem && touch /tmp/eval-act-0/cli.js
evals.expected_output: Step 2 is executed. progress updated to 2/3. code-map.mem gets an entry for the file touched. No failures recorded.

assertions.text: .memplan/progress shows step 2 as complete (e.g. '2/3')
.memplan/memory/code-map.mem contains an entry for a file touched during the step
.memplan/memory/failures.mem is empty (step succeeded)

evals.description: Pre-flight halt: dep step 1 is not yet complete. Verifies the skill halts without executing the step.
evals.expected_output: Skill halts with a message indicating step 2 cannot start because dep step 1 is not complete. No files are modified.

assertions.text: Output contains a warning that step 2 cannot start due to unmet dep
.memplan/progress still shows '0/3 | not-started'

evals.description: Pre-flight halt: steps.mem is missing. Verifies the skill halts immediately with the correct message.
evals.expected_output: Skill halts immediately with a message that steps.mem is absent. No execution occurs.

assertions.text: Output contains a message about missing steps.mem and instructs running memplan/plan
No files outside .memplan/ are created or modified

evals.description: Entities accumulate correctly across sessions: each act invocation appends new entity entries to entities.mem without overwriting previous ones.
evals.setup:
mkdir -p /tmp/eval-act-3/.memplan/memory /tmp/eval-act-3/.memplan/decisions /tmp/eval-act-3/.memplan/inbox && echo "0/2 | not-started" > /tmp/eval-act-3/.memplan/progress && printf "+step:id=1,text=create-user-service,atomic=true
+step:id=2,text=create-order-service,atomic=true
" > /tmp/eval-act-3/.memplan/steps.mem && printf "" > /tmp/eval-act-3/.memplan/memory/entities.mem && printf "" > /tmp/eval-act-3/.memplan/memory/code-map.mem && printf "" > /tmp/eval-act-3/.memplan/memory/failures.mem && printf "" > /tmp/eval-act-3/.memplan/stale.mem && touch /tmp/eval-act-3/user-service.ts /tmp/eval-act-3/order-service.ts
evals.expected_output: After both steps are acted on, entities.mem contains entries for both UserService and OrderService. The first entity entry is not overwritten when the second is appended.

assertions.text: .memplan/memory/entities.mem contains at least two distinct entity entries after both steps execute
The entity entry recorded during step 1 still exists in entities.mem after step 2 runs
.memplan/progress shows 2/2 after both steps complete

evals.description: Entity dedup: same entity must not be appended twice. Re-running act on the same step should not create duplicate entity entries.

evals.expected_output: entities.mem still contains exactly one UserService entry after the run.

assertions.text: .memplan/memory/entities.mem contains exactly one entry for UserService after the skill runs
The skill explicitly checks for existing entity entries before appending (output or behaviour confirms dedup)

evals.prompt: Act on step 3 (which has been refined into sub-steps).
evals.description: Phase 3 sub-step execution: when a step is marked refined=true, act must execute its sub-steps (3.1, 3.2, 3.3) in order instead of executing the parent step directly.
evals.setup:
mkdir -p /tmp/eval-act-8/.memplan/memory /tmp/eval-act-8/.memplan/decisions /tmp/eval-act-8/.memplan/inbox /tmp/eval-act-8/references && echo '2/5 | step-2-complete' > /tmp/eval-act-8/.memplan/progress && printf '+step:id=1,text=init-project,atomic=true
+step:id=2,text=write-core-module,atomic=true
+step:id=3,text=implement-dual-file-write-helper,refined=true
+step:id=3.1,text=write-references-dual-file-write-md,atomic=true
+step:id=3.2,text=add-generated-file-header,deps=3.1,atomic=true
+step:id=3.3,text=verify-helper-invoked,deps=3.1|3.2,atomic=true
+step:id=4,text=write-tests,deps=3,atomic=true
' > /tmp/eval-act-8/.memplan/steps.mem && touch /tmp/eval-act-8/.memplan/memory/code-map.mem /tmp/eval-act-8/.memplan/memory/entities.mem /tmp/eval-act-8/.memplan/memory/failures.mem && printf '' > /tmp/eval-act-8/.memplan/stale.mem && printf '' > /tmp/eval-act-8/.memplan/deps.mem && printf '' > /tmp/eval-act-8/.memplan/deps-closure.mem && touch /tmp/eval-act-8/references/dual-file-write.md /tmp/eval-act-8/header.ts
evals.expected_output: When act processes step 3 (marked refined=true), it executes sub-steps 3.1, 3.2, 3.3 in sequence rather than the parent step. Progress advances through each sub-step: 3/5 (after 3.1), 4/5 (after 3.2), 5/5 (after 3.3). Step 3 itself is never directly executed.

assertions.text: All three sub-steps (3.1, 3.2, 3.3) are executed in order when act is invoked on step 3
The parent step 3 text ('implement-dual-file-write-helper') is NOT executed directly — only sub-steps run
.memplan/progress advances through 3/5, 4/5, 5/5 as sub-steps complete (not skipping from 2/5 to 5/5)
Sub-step 3.2 waits for 3.1 to complete before running (deps=3.1 is honored)
.memplan/memory/code-map.mem contains entries for files touched in sub-steps 3.1 and 3.2

evals.prompt: Continue acting on step 3 (refined step with sub-steps, where 3.1 is already complete).
evals.description: Resume refined-step execution: when sub-step 3.1 is already complete, act must skip it and resume from 3.2. Verifies the progress text is parsed correctly to determine the last completed sub-step.
evals.setup:
mkdir -p /tmp/eval-act-9/.memplan/memory /tmp/eval-act-9/.memplan/decisions /tmp/eval-act-9/.memplan/inbox && echo '3/5 | write-references-dual-file-write-md' > /tmp/eval-act-9/.memplan/progress && printf '+step:id=1,text=init-project,atomic=true
+step:id=2,text=write-core-module,atomic=true
+step:id=3,text=implement-dual-file-write-helper,refined=true
+step:id=3.1,text=write-references-dual-file-write-md,atomic=true
+step:id=3.2,text=add-generated-file-header,deps=3.1,atomic=true
+step:id=3.3,text=verify-helper-invoked,deps=3.2,atomic=true
+step:id=4,text=write-tests,deps=3,atomic=true
' > /tmp/eval-act-9/.memplan/steps.mem && printf '+file:path=references/dual-file-write.md,purpose=reference,touched=~2024-01-01
' > /tmp/eval-act-9/.memplan/memory/code-map.mem && touch /tmp/eval-act-9/.memplan/memory/entities.mem /tmp/eval-act-9/.memplan/memory/failures.mem && printf '' > /tmp/eval-act-9/.memplan/stale.mem && printf '' > /tmp/eval-act-9/.memplan/deps.mem && printf '' > /tmp/eval-act-9/.memplan/deps-closure.mem && touch /tmp/eval-act-9/references/dual-file-write.md /tmp/eval-act-9/header.ts
evals.expected_output: Act reads progress (3/5 | write-references-dual-file-write-md), identifies that sub-step 3.1 is complete, skips it, and resumes from 3.2. Progress advances from 3/5 to 4/5 (after 3.2), then 5/5 (after 3.3). Finally, parent step 3 is marked complete.

assertions.text: Sub-step 3.1 is NOT re-executed — the agent correctly identifies it as complete from the progress text
Sub-step 3.2 is executed (the first incomplete sub-step after 3.1)
.memplan/progress advances from 3/5 to 4/5 (after 3.2), not from 3/5 to 2/5 or 3/5
After sub-step 3.3 completes, progress is updated with the parent step 3 text to mark the parent complete

+step:id=3,text=implement-dual-file-write-helper,refined=true
+step:id=3.1,text=write-references-dual-file-write-md,atomic=true
+step:id=3.2,text=run-failing-command,atomic=true
+step:id=3.3,text=verify-helper-invoked,deps=3.2,atomic=true
+step:id=4,text=write-tests,deps=3,atomic=true
' > /tmp/eval-act-10/.memplan/steps.mem && printf '+file:path=references/dual-file-write.md,purpose=reference,touched=~2024-01-01
' > /tmp/eval-act-10/.memplan/memory/code-map.mem && touch /tmp/eval-act-10/.memplan/memory/entities.mem /tmp/eval-act-10/.memplan/memory/failures.mem && printf '' > /tmp/eval-act-10/.memplan/stale.mem && printf '' > /tmp/eval-act-10/.memplan/deps.mem && printf '' > /tmp/eval-act-10/.memplan/deps-closure.mem && printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash

' > /tmp/eval-act-10/fail-command.sh && chmod +x /tmp/eval-act-10/fail-command.sh
evals.expected_output: Act resumes from sub-step 3.2 (since 3.1 is complete). Sub-step 3.2 involves running a command that fails. Act records the failure in failures.mem, halts, and does NOT proceed to sub-step 3.3. Progress remains at 3/5.

assertions.text: .memplan/memory/failures.mem contains a +failure: entry with cmd and reason fields for sub-step 3.2
Sub-step 3.3 is NOT executed — act halts after the 3.2 failure
.memplan/progress remains at 3/5 — it is not advanced to 4/5 when sub-step 3.2 fails
Output contains a message like 'Sub-step 3.2 failed — failure recorded. Resolve before continuing with remaining sub-steps.'
